title: Reading Assembly Request (M3)
description: Successor to M0's readingAssemblyRequest, promoted out of reading-evidence.schema.json into its own document and renamed assemblyRequest. Two changes from M0. (1) The required reading_key — whose pattern embeds the raw application user id, and whose canonical M0 fixture reads literally 'user:usr_01JAMPLEUSER00000001:2026-07-30:release-12' — is replaced by the opaque content-addressed assembly_id from assembly-identity.schema.json. This object is the model-boundary object: it carries output_schema and approved_fragments and states that the assembler may not introduce fragments outside that set, so spec section 10's prohibition on stable direct identifiers applies to it directly. (2) facts and approved_fragments lose minItems: 1. M0 made both non-empty and required, which makes the commonest day of all — no cycle inside orb — unrepresentable, and with it the reviewed universal fallback path that such a day must take.

id.description: Calculated fact id only. Never raw health, full calendar, or raw journal bodies.

framing.description: Minimal framing signal only (e.g. a domain preference id), not raw private content.

assembly_id.description: Content-addressed, not user-addressed. Nothing that names a person crosses this boundary, and because the preimage carries the day's fact set the same user gets an unrelated id each day.

facts.description: May be empty: a day with no eligible calculated fact still assembles, and takes the reviewed universal fallback.

approved_fragments.description: Eligible editorial fragment ids from DER-18. The assembler may not introduce fragments outside this set. May be empty for the same reason facts may be empty; the fallback copy is resolved from the release's locale-bound daily_fallback rather than from this list.

assemblyRequest.$comment: additionalProperties:false is the mechanical half of the boundary rule — reading_key, user_id, chart_fingerprint, local_date, target_timezone, and generation_anchor are rejected because they are simply not declared. The other half is a serialization test asserting that neither 'usr_' nor 'cs_' appears anywhere in the encoded request.
